title: Adding a non-tree edge creates a cycle
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $T$ be a spanning tree of $G$: a connected, acyclic subgraph of $G$ that touches every vertex. If $e$ is an edge of $G$ that does not lie in $T$, then the graph $T + e$ obtained by adjoining $e$ to $T$ contains a cycle, i.e. there is a vertex $u$ and a closed walk from $u$ to itself in $T + e$ that is a cycle.
